prompt: You're kicking off a project with a sociable, enthusiastic teammate who loves big ideas.
tells: sociable, enthusiastic teammate who loves big ideas
why: Start with the vision and energy, brainstorm together, and keep it friendly.
trap: Starting with the risk register suits C.

prompt: A charismatic colleague agrees to everything in meetings but often forgets the details.
why: Keep the conversation upbeat, then follow up in writing with the key details and dates.
trap: Long written specs up front suit C; i needs the talk, then a short written follow-up.

prompt: A teammate who thrives on recognition just finished a big push.
trap: Private, low-key thanks suits S better.

prompt: You need to give critical feedback to an upbeat, people-focused colleague who worries about being liked.
why: Keep it warm and personal, show you value them, then be clear on the change, and agree next steps together.
trap: Blunt, results-only feedback suits D, and could crush an i.

prompt: You want an energetic, persuasive manager to champion your idea to other teams.
why: Make it exciting: tell the story and show who it helps and how it'll look.
trap: A spreadsheet of costs suits C.

prompt: A meeting includes an expressive teammate who likes to talk ideas through out loud.
tells: likes to talk ideas through out loud
why: Leave room for discussion and ideas, then summarize decisions in writing.
trap: Sending a dense pre-read and expecting silence suits C.

prompt: An optimistic teammate keeps missing deadlines while juggling lots of exciting projects.
why: Agree on clear dates together, keep it positive, and check in socially but often.
trap: Taking over the decisions suits nobody, and is a D habit.

prompt: A new hire is outgoing, chatty and wants to meet everyone.
why: Introduce them around and let them learn through people.
trap: A quiet week with documentation suits C.

prompt: Write to a colleague who signs every email with emojis and exclamation marks.
why: Match some of the warmth and keep it friendly, with key points easy to spot.

prompt: You need an enthusiastic sales lead to adopt a new CRM process.
why: Show how it makes them look good and helps their relationships, and make it fun to try.
trap: Walking through the compliance rationale suits C.
